title: Key & door
evidenceStatus: 240 decoded episode rows: 156 wins, 83 lab cutoffs, one provider interruption; 7,933 trace rows and 129 observations. Offline record/source/React-element probe only.
summary: The route is a recorded-action viewer, with no playable engine, manual movement, or Jev handoff. Its 64-action cutoff differs from native MiniGrid limits and its traces omit resulting terminal states. Build a complete local maze campaign, then evaluate Jev in a separate seeded comparison with explicit information aids, native rules, and strong code baselines.
strengths: Real MiniGrid execution records rewards, partial observations, action latency, and cache flags; the visible BFS comparator does not see a privileged full map.
Observation interning has a lossless round-trip test, and exact-observation decision reuse has a contract test.
README and result notes disclose the 64-step limit, shared decisions, repeated Empty layout, and superior geometric baseline; the UI identifies recorded playback and excludes the interrupted episode.

findings.title: There is no complete playable game
findings.evidence: experience-prototypes/src/games.tsx:66, :124. All controls select episodes or move a trace index; no game transition, manual action, live request, handoff, loss, new maze, or actual state restart exists.
findings.impact: The current replay matches its Watch copy but cannot deliver the user's requested full-game experience or demonstrate assistance in a live position.
findings.fix: Build a complete local manual maze with real win/loss/restart first. Route Jev and code policies through the same action dispatcher; separate Play, Recorded runs, and Compare. Provider failure returns control without ending play.

findings.title: Terminal state and stopping reasons are missing
findings.evidence: src/jev_lab/games.py:147 stores pre-action state with post-action reward and no next observation or termination flags. All 156 wins end with the goal still in front; 83 runs stop at the lab's 64-action cutoff. Native MiniGrid 3.1.0 limits are 100 Empty/250 DoorKey actions. The interrupted row counts 22 actions plus an error as 23 steps.
findings.impact: Replays never show the winning state, and goal failure, artificial cutoff, and provider unavailability cannot be treated as the same game outcome.
findings.fix: Store initial and resulting states, reward, executed action count, termination/truncation, and explicit goal/timeout/loss/cutoff/provider/user-stop reasons. Show the final board and report scheduled versus completed outcomes separately.

findings.title: Repeated layouts and shared cache limit the memory comparison
findings.evidence: src/jev_lab/games.py:113, :193. Empty's 30 seeds share one initial observation and one action trace per deterministic policy. Jev reuses cached decisions on 3,886 of 4,298 action rows (90.4%); 419 memoized request states are shared. DoorKey has 20 distinct initial observations, which are not necessarily 20 full worlds.
findings.impact: The existing results describe a small cached policy and do not estimate fresh-call variability or general navigation performance from 30 independent environments.
findings.fix: Keep fixed Empty as a diagnostic, use held-out generated layouts and request IDs, compare against a persistent observed-map planner, and separate uncached policy evaluation from cached system performance. Cluster uncertainty by unique layout.

findings.title: The assisted wrapper changes the benchmark and misnames toggle
findings.evidence: src/jev_lab/games.py:12, :15, :37. Text labels, inventory, and a five-action mask replace native seven-action interaction. open_door maps to toggle and is offered on open doors or without a key. Recorded random actions close an already open door ten times and try locked doors without a key 20 times.
findings.impact: The comparison is an assisted symbolic MiniGrid protocol, not a vision or unmodified action-space benchmark; action names can misdescribe actual consequences.
findings.fix: Use accurate toggle semantics, version the observation/action wrapper, and report native versus assisted tracks separately. Match information across competing policies and label privileged oracles as ceilings.

findings.title: Replay hides door status and the memory input
findings.evidence: experience-prototypes/src/games.tsx:34, :55, :241. Actual element trees are identical for locked/open doors and yellow/red doors. The inspector omits recent_actions even though src/jev_lab/games.py:103 supplies it to the memory policy.
findings.impact: Visitors cannot see whether a door changed state or inspect the exact history that supposedly improved the decision. Color is currently a future-extension issue because these worlds use yellow doors.
findings.fix: Render door state distinctly, show exact request history and inventory, distinguish pre-decision versus resulting frames, and provide understandable keyboard/touch controls and state feedback for play.

simulation.title: A complete three-room key maze with manual and Jev control
simulation.description: A seedable three-level campaign has corridors, matching keys/doors, treasure, hazards, fog, and exits. Three hearts provide a real loss condition; hazards cost a heart and return the player to the level entrance while preserving collected items/opened doors. Final exit wins the campaign. Restart resets level state, and new game changes the seed. Human play, one-move suggestions, Jev takeover, and immediate manual takeover all use the same engine. This custom game is separate from literal MiniGrid evaluation.
simulation.jevsRole: Choose one action from the declared contract using only current partial observation and the selected history/map mode. Pending answers are invalidated on human takeover, restart, revision change, or terminal state. No map edits, teleports, score changes, or rule changes.
simulation.codeRole: Maintain serializable seed, map/object state, pose, inventory, hearts, turns, fog/history, controller, lifecycle, and revision. A pure transition function handles collisions, keys, locks, hazards, respawn, exit progression, win/loss, and reset. The observation adapter excludes hidden state from model requests.
acceptanceCriteria: Without a provider key, a visitor can start, play, win or lose, restart, and begin a new campaign using keyboard or touch.
Key matching, door passage, hazard damage/respawn, lives, level progression, and final victory follow documented rules and expose their effects.
Each action applies at most once; takeover, restart, seed change, and terminal states reject pending answers.
The assistant receives only declared information; a labeled spectator map never leaks through the adapter.
Seed plus action list reproduces state hashes and terminal outcome; the final board is visible and restart resets all relevant state.
Game outcome, provider interruption, comparison-budget suspension, and user stop remain distinct; manual play can continue without the provider.

evaluation.design: First validate the custom game on 100 seeds in each of three difficulty tiers, four code policies per layout (1,200 complete local episodes), and 1,000 generated lifecycle/handoff schedules. Require zero accepted stale actions, exact replay, and demonstrated manual win/loss/restart/handoff. Separately define 30 held-out seeds per each of four official DoorKey sizes, totaling 120 environment/seed pairs. Six policies and native/assisted tracks yield 1,440 episodes, including 480 Jev episodes and at most 457,200 logical requests before retries under native 250/360/640/2,560 step limits. A five-seed 5x5 development pilot across two Jev policies/two tracks is 20 episodes and at most 5,000 calls. Disable cross-episode cache for fresh-call policy evaluation and separately measure cached operation. Report native return, goal rate, all-scheduled availability, stop reasons, actions, loops, path efficiency, latency, and cost. Use 10,000 paired bootstrap resamples clustered by unique generated layout, stratified by size; memory-improvement claims require a paired 95% interval above zero. A separate 24-player counterbalanced handoff study has 96 full games, with two manual/two assisted per player and at most 2,400 assistant calls; the assistant budget returns control without ending play. All proposed runs remain unperformed.
baselines: Uniform random actions under the same declared action information within each track.
Current visible-grid BFS, retaining the strong existing comparator.
Persistent observed-map frontier/path planner with an explicit memory budget and the same observations.
Reactive Jev versus Jev with eight recent actions, differing only in the declared history ablation.
Privileged full-map shortest-path oracle, labeled as a ceiling rather than an equal-information competitor.
Manual-only versus optional Jev handoff in a separate counterbalanced human study.
metrics: Native mean terminal return and goal success, with paired layout-clustered uncertainty and separate size strata.
All-scheduled completion, provider interruption, lab/budget suspension, and explicit termination/truncation reason.
Executed actions, cycles/no-progress, repeated toggles, and success-conditioned path efficiency versus the labeled oracle.
Request count, cache hits, fresh-call/end-to-end latency, retries, and cost.
Stale-action acceptance, deterministic replay, correct terminal state, restart completeness, and keyboard/touch lifecycle success.
Human completion/time, mistakes, takeovers, actual assistant use, and preserved state during handoff.

coverage.current: Two official MiniGrid configurations, one of four DoorKey sizes and one of six Empty configurations; 30 seed labels each across four policies yield 240 rows. Modified text/action-mask protocol and 64-action cap; fixed Empty repeats one layout. 156 wins, 83 lab cutoffs, one interruption. No fixed external dataset split or full-suite percentage is claimed.
coverage.full: MiniGrid procedurally generates environments and has no finite official test split asserted here. Proposed local manifest covers all four DoorKey sizes with 30 held-out seeds each, six policies, and two information tracks: 1,440 episodes. Separate authored custom-game and human-handoff protocols cover complete play rather than truncated traces.
coverage.feasibility: Future work requires terminal-complete logs, pinned environment/wrapper versions, new disjoint seeds, browser-port parity if used, human participants, and substantial provider budget. The full comparison has a 457,200-request worst-case ceiling; the declared pilot caps at 5,000. Provider budgets suspend rather than falsify game outcomes. No large data/weight download is needed; no new model or environment episodes were run.

libraries.name: MiniGrid
libraries.use: Retain the authoritative seeded reference environment for literal comparison. Verify any browser port against state-transition fixtures before sharing its name or scores. Jev is a policy, not the game rules.

libraries.name: Phaser
libraries.use: Optional scene lifecycle, keyboard/touch input, and animation for the complete custom maze. Keep deterministic turn transitions independent of rendering and frame rate; the existing React grid can support a small initial version.

libraries.name: Gymnasium
libraries.use: Explicit reset/step/reward/termination/truncation contract for the comparison adapter, separating completed game outcomes from stopped traces and provider interruption.

nextSteps.action: Correct outcome categories, executed action counts, toggle naming, and assisted-protocol labels.
Record resulting observations and terminal flags, display final state, and expose exact memory inputs.
Build the complete manual maze campaign with deterministic transitions, real win/loss, restart, and seed controls.
Add Jev suggestion/takeover through the same engine with immediate manual takeover and revision checks.
Create separate seeded comparison mode with matched information, strong code baselines, native/assisted tracks, and the declared pilot before expensive full runs.
Distinguish door status and inventory visually and verify keyboard/touch feedback; later reuse the engine for semantic object/hazard missions.
